source.title: Improved Regularization and Robustness for Fine-tuning in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports fine-tuning results where explicit layer-wise regularization reduces the training–test accuracy gap, including under noisy labels. This refines the claim's regularization account in transfer learning; it does not test the central random-label memorization and natural-label generalization result.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported train/test gap changes and measured properties of fine-tuned networks. Table 2 and other benchmark comparisons report test accuracy, but do not isolate the claim's generalization-gap behavior, so they are not separate rows. The paper's discussion of memorizing random labels cites prior work; that cited result is not this study's own result.
record.test_reason: The study tests distance regularization and self-labeling for transfer learning, not any listed claim version. Its Gaussian perturbed training losses are neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor a test of sharpness ranking generalization gaps. Partially corrupted labels and overfitting curves do not establish V1's near-perfect random-label fit and natural-versus-random held-out comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive a PAC-Bayes bound involving distance from pre-trained weights and noise stability, empirically examine these quantities, and propose layer-wise regularization combined with label correction and reweighting to improve fine-tuning accuracy and robustness to label noise. They do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness-gap correlation.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines transfer fine-tuning from pre-trained models with layerwise distance constraints and noisy labels, rather than the claim's random-label memorization and natural-label generalization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and initialization affect the measured layerwise distances and perturbed losses; layer location affects distance from initialization. For noisy-label fine-tuning, noise rate and applying regularization affect the training-test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned weights stay relatively close to pre-trained weights, with greater movement in higher layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer fine-tuning produces layer-dependent distances from initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-trained initializations yield lower Gaussian perturbed training losses than random initialization; adversarial pre-training sometimes lowers them further.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-training can improve the noise stability of fine-tuned models under fixed, unscaled Gaussian weight perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise distance constraints reduce the training-test accuracy gap and improve test accuracy on MIT-Indoor with 60% and 80% label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distance regularization can reduce overfitting during transfer fine-tuning with corrupted target labels.

record.problems: The training-test gap comparisons are shown as plots without numeric values in the supplied text. Perturbed-loss results use loss after Gaussian weight perturbations and are measured on the training set; they do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness relation to generalization gaps. Several table values are presented within a flattened layout and lack explicit row-level text descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2, Tables 3–7 and Table 11 report test accuracy/AUROC comparisons for fine-tuning methods and ablations, but do not isolate a version's named behavior or measure its specified gap relation; therefore they are not extracted as rows. Figure 5 and Table 9 report self-label correction precision and relabel counts, not a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, and chance held-out performance under random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus an equal number of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 3b's flattened layout caused dataset and initialization assignments to be mixed. Its first block is CUB-200-2011 and its second block is Indoor, each with Random, Pre-trained, and Adversarial columns. Missing cells from this related measurement are not missing tests of a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting random labels and comparing held-out natural-label versus random-label performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Adam is used in experiments, but the study does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for generalization.

The study measures layerwise distance and perturbed loss as generalization-related quantities, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness, compare the stated norm- and margin-based measures, or rank generalization gaps across networks.
No removal of memorized training examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 (pre-trained on ImageNet)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Frobenius distance from pre-trained weights, relative to pre-trained weight norm, by layer.
rows.measure: Ratio of fine-tuned distance to pre-trained weights’ ℓ2 norm, by layer
rows.note: Text says distances were relatively small and varied by layer, with smaller distances at lower layers and larger ones at higher layers. This is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure or a comparison of gaps required by V7.
rows.check: Distance traveled from initialization, normalized by pre-trained weight norm, does not measure V7's perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps.
